mainTopic: Seizing a dead debtor's property, a messenger's liability, relying on one trusted person in court, and writing court documents before the fact
overview: The amud opens by finishing רב נחמן's ruling about a boat grabbed for a dead man's debts. רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע then grab the boat themselves. רבא rejects their grab, quoting רב נחמן that seizing for a debt works only while the debtor is alive. Next, a messenger pays אבימי's debt without getting the שטר back. רבי אבהו believes the lenders through a מיגו, and the גמרא rules that the messenger must repay the sender. A woman holding a bag of documents loses them to the heirs, because her grab counts as after death. רבא relies on בת רב חסדא, whom he knows with certainty, but not on רב פפא as a single witness. The גמרא then concludes that such a witness can only weaken a document. Finally, רב פפי attacks רב ביבי בר אביי for writing a document of rights before an oath. The גמרא rejects רבא's rule behind that attack and starts a proof from רבי יוחנן that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of רב נחמן's ruling: he did not acquire
steps.stepSummary: The text opens with the last words of רב נחמן's ruling: the man who grabbed the boat for the creditor did not acquire it.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...has not acquired it.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of a ruling that started just before this section. The ruling is that someone who grabs property for a creditor, in a way that hurts other creditors, does not acquire it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The helper grabbed the boat for one creditor, but that would take it away from other people who were also owed money. A person cannot act for someone else in a way that harms third parties, so his grab does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not acquire it; the acquisition does not take effect

phrases.english: has not acquired it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ruling begun before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who seizes for a creditor where it harms other creditors does not acquire.

steps.title: The two חכמים grab the boat themselves
steps.stepSummary: Since the helper's grab failed, רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, who were also owed money, grab the boat themselves. Each one claims he acquired the entire boat.
steps.simpleTranslation: They themselves seized it. רב פפא steered it with an oar, and רב הונא son of רב יהושע pulled it with a rope. One said: I acquired all of it. The other said: I acquired all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The two חכמים, who were also owed money by the dead man, physically take the boat, and each claims all of it for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each one did a different physical act on the boat: one rowed it and one pulled it. That raises two questions: did either of them acquire it, and if so, which one? The next steps deal with whether this grab works at all.

keyTerms.meaning: An oar (he steered with an oar)

phrases.english: They themselves seized it.
phrases.notes: "They" means רב פפא and רב הונא, who were also owed money by the dead man.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa steered it with an oar.
Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
pulled it with a rope.

phrases.aramaic: מָר אָמַר: אֲנָא קָנֵינָא לַהּ לְכוּלַּהּ,
phrases.english: One said: I acquired all of it,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר אָמַר: אֲנָא קָנֵינָא לַהּ לְכוּלַּהּ.
phrases.english: and the other said: I acquired all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the helper's seizure fails, the creditors seize for themselves
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each creditor claims to have acquired the whole boat by his own act of seizing.

steps.title: רב פנחס בר אמי challenges them with the rule of רב ושמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב פנחס בר אמי says that, according to רב ושמואל, grabbing only works when the items are piled up and lying in a public place. This boat was not lying in such a place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פנחס בר אמי met them and said to them: רב and שמואל both say: and this applies only when the items are piled up and lying in the public domain!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone meets the two חכמים and challenges their grab. He quotes a rule from רב ושמואל that seems to say their grab should not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ושמואל limit the rule of "whoever grabs first gets it" to items lying in a pile in רשות הרבים, where nobody holds them. The challenge is that this boat was not lying in a public place, so grabbing it should not help.

keyTerms.meaning: He met them; came across them

phrases.aramaic: פְּגַע בְּהוּ רַב פִּנְחָס בַּר אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: Rav Pinchas bar Ami met them,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
phrases.english: he said to them: Rav and Shmuel both say
and this applies only when they are piled up and lying in the public domain!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ וְהוּא שֶׁצְּבוּרִין וּמוּנָּחִין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the validity of the seizure in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The two חכמים' claim that their seizure of the boat counts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב ושמואל limit seizing to items piled in the public domain, and the boat was not in such a place.

steps.title: They answer: we grabbed it in the middle of the river
steps.stepSummary: The two חכמים answer that they also grabbed the boat in a public place, because they took it from the strong current in the middle of the river.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We too seized it from the current of the river.
steps.whatsHappening: The two חכמים defend their grab. They say their case does fit רב ושמואל's condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle of the river, where the current is strong, counts as רשות הרבים. So the boat was in a public place when they took it, which meets the condition רב פנחס quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: The strong current of the river, its middle part

phrases.english: They said to him: We too
seized it from the current of the river.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פנחס בר אמי's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual answer showing the case fits the condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The boat was not in the public domain, so the seizure fails
steps.terutzMaskana: The river's current counts as public domain, so the condition is met

steps.title: רבא rejects their grab: seizing only works while the debtor is alive
steps.stepSummary: They come to רבא, who scolds them sharply and quotes רב נחמן: grabbing for a debt only works if it was done while the debtor was still alive. Here the debtor had already died, so their grab is worthless.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came before רבא. He said to them: White geese, who strip off people's cloaks! This is what רב נחמן said: And this applies only when he seized it while the debtor was alive.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rules against both of them and says neither one acquired the boat. He backs this up with a statement of רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question of which of them acquired more falls away, because רבא says the grab never worked at all. Once the debtor died the boat already belonged to his heirs, so grabbing it afterward is like taking someone's cloak. Being in the public domain does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: White geese, a jab at their white beards
Who strip off cloaks; who take what isn't theirs

phrases.english: They came before Rava,
he said to them: White geese,
phrases.notes: A sharp jab at the two older חכמים with their white beards.

phrases.english: who strip off people's cloaks!
This is what Rav Nachman said:
And this applies only when he seized it while he was alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: וְהוּא שֶׁתְּפָסָהּ מֵחַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overrides the defense in step 4 with a further condition
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole seizure by both חכמים, not only the question of who got more
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The seizure happened after the debtor's death, when seizing no longer works
steps.whatToRemember: Grabbing a debtor's property for your debt works only if done while he is alive and the items are in a public place. After death, neither creditor could grab the boat.
steps.confusionAlert: Being in רשות הרבים was not enough. רבא adds a second condition, that the debtor be alive, and that is what defeats them.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows there are two separate conditions for seizing: the place (רב ושמואל) and the time (רב נחמן).

steps.title: A new story: אבימי sends money to pay his debt
steps.stepSummary: אבימי son of רבי אבהו owed money to people in בי חוזאי. He sent the money with חמא, who paid it and then asked for the loan document back.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבימי son of רבי אבהו owed money to people in בי חוזאי. He sent the money with חמא son of רבה בר אבהו. He went and paid them, and said to them: Give me the document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about paying back a debt through a messenger. This is setup for the problem that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The messenger pays and naturally asks for the loan document, so the lenders can't collect again with it. The question will be whether the payment really went toward the debt in that document.

keyTerms.meaning: They were owed money by him

phrases.english: Avimi son of Rabbi Abbahu

phrases.aramaic: הֲווֹ מַסְּקִי בֵּיהּ זוּזֵי בֵּי חוֹזָאֵי,
phrases.english: owed money to people in Bei Chozai,

phrases.aramaic: שַׁדְּרִינְהוּ בְּיַד חָמָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר אֲבָהוּ.
phrases.english: he sent it with Chama son of Rabba bar Abbahu.
He went and paid them.
He said to them: Give me the document.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבִימִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ הֲווֹ מַסְּקִי בֵּיהּ זוּזֵי בֵּי חוֹזָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new, separate story about debt payment
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup: a messenger paid a debt and asked for the loan document back.

steps.title: The lenders say the money was for a different debt
steps.stepSummary: The lenders refuse to hand over the document. They say the money paid was for other debts that were never written down.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: They are side debts.
steps.whatsHappening: The lenders answer the messenger's request with a claim: the payment went toward other, unwritten debts, not the debt in the document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they are believed, the debt in the document is still unpaid and they can keep the document. This sets up the question the גמרא will deal with next: are they believed?

keyTerms.meaning: Side debts; other loans not written in a document

phrases.english: They said to him: They are side debts.
phrases.notes: They mean the money covered a different loan that had no document, so this one is still owed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the messenger's demand for the document
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The messenger asks for the loan document after paying
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lenders claim the payment was for other, unwritten debts, so they will keep the document.

steps.title: רבי אבהו asks whether there were witnesses to the payment
steps.stepSummary: The case comes before רבי אבהו. He asks חמא whether he has witnesses that he paid the lenders, and חמא says no.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רבי אבהו. רבי אבהו asked him: Do you have witnesses that you paid them? He said: No.
steps.whatsHappening: The dispute over the unreturned שטר reaches רבי אבהו. He first checks the facts by asking whether anyone saw the payment, which sets up his ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether there were witnesses decides everything here. With witnesses, the lenders could not deny that money changed hands. Without them, the lenders' word carries extra weight, as the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: He came before him (brought the case to a judge)

phrases.english: He came before Rabbi Abbahu.
phrases.notes: The one who came is חמא, the messenger from the last step who paid the money.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִית לְךָ סָהֲדֵי דִּפְרַעְתִּינְהוּ?
phrases.english: He said to him: Do you have witnesses that you paid them?
He said to him: No.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the lenders' refusal from step 7 to a judge, who checks the facts.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether there were witnesses to the payment

steps.title: The lenders are believed because they could have denied everything
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו rules with a מיגו. Since the lenders could have claimed they were never paid at all, they are believed when they say the money went to other, unwritten debts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Since they could have said 'this never happened at all,' they can also say 'it was for side debts.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives his ruling: the lenders win and keep the שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no witnesses, the lenders could have flatly denied getting any money. They chose a smaller claim instead, saying they got the money but it paid off other debts. A person who could have made a stronger claim is believed when he makes a weaker one. This is the logic of מיגו.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since': a person is believed on one claim because he could have made a better one
These things never happened at all (a total denial)
Side debts: other loans that had no שטר

steps.confusionAlert: The lenders admit they took the money, yet they still win. That is because no one can prove it, so their admission is voluntary. It actually helps them through the מיגו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic example of מיגו, a basic tool of believing a litigant that comes up all over ש״ס.

phrases.english: He said to him: Since they are able to say
'These things never happened,'
phrases.notes: He means they could have claimed they never got any money from you.

phrases.english: they are also able to say 'they are side debts.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the 'no witnesses' answer from step 8 to rule for the lenders.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Without witnesses to the payment, the lenders are believed through a מיגו that the money paid for other debts, so they keep the שטר.

steps.title: Must the messenger repay the sender?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the שליח, who paid without first getting the שטר back, must repay the sender's loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding the messenger paying back, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the sender has lost money, the גמרא asks whether the שליח who caused it must make up the loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חמא handed over the money before taking back the שטר, and that is what let the lenders keep it. The question is whether this mistake makes him responsible to the person who sent him.

phrases.english: Regarding the messenger paying, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a follow-up question that comes out of the ruling in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the שליח must repay the sender for the lost money

steps.title: רב אשי: it depends on the order of the instructions
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the answer depends on the wording. If the sender said 'take the שטר and give the money,' the שליח pays. If he said 'give the money and take the שטר,' the שליח does not pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We look at it. If he told him 'take the document and give the money,' he pays. If he said 'give the money and take the document,' he does not pay.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question by looking at the order of the sender's instructions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sender mentioned taking the שטר first, the שליח went against his instructions by paying first, so he is responsible. If the sender mentioned paying first, the שליח did exactly what he was told, so he is not responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: We look at it, we check

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: We see,
if he said to him
'Take the document and give money,' he pays.
'Give money and take the document,' he does not pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שליח pays only if the instructions put taking the שטר first.

steps.title: The messenger always pays
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב אשי. Either way the שליח pays, because the sender can say 'I sent you to help me, not to hurt me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not so. Either way he pays, because the sender can say to him: 'I sent you to fix things for me, not to ruin them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב אשי's split answer and rules that the שליח is always responsible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of the words does not matter. A שליח is only sent to act in the sender's best interest. Paying without making sure the שטר comes back is a harmful act, and the sender never authorized that.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is not so (the גמרא rejects a view)
I sent you to fix things, not to ruin them

steps.whatToRemember: A שליח is sent to help the sender, never to hurt him. If he causes a loss by paying without getting the שטר back, he must pay, no matter how the instructions were worded.
steps.whyThisMatters: 'לתקוני שדרתיך ולא לעוותי' is a basic rule about the limits of שליחות, and it is used in many other places.

phrases.english: And that is not so;
either this way or that way, he pays.
For he can say to him: 'I sent you to fix things'
'and not to ruin them.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's distinction from step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole split answer of רב אשי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wording does not matter, because a שליח is never authorized to cause the sender a loss.

steps.title: A woman holding a bag of documents says she grabbed it while the owner was alive
steps.stepSummary: A woman had a bag of documents left with her. The יורשים demand it back, and she says she grabbed it for a debt while the owner was still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman had a bag of documents deposited with her. The heirs came and demanded it from her. She told them: I grabbed them while he was alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story that connects to the rule about grabbing for a debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She is not denying that the bag belonged to the dead man. She claims she took hold of it for a debt during his lifetime, which would make her grab valid. The earlier rule (step 5) says grabbing only works while the debtor is alive.

phrases.english: There was a certain woman with whom were deposited
a bag of documents.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתוֹ יוֹרְשִׁים קָא תָּבְעִי לֵיהּ מִינַּהּ.
phrases.english: The heirs came and were demanding it from her.
She said to them: I grabbed them while he was alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דַּהֲווֹ מִיפַּקְדִי גַּבַּהּ מְלוּגָא דִשְׁטָרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case connected to the rule about grabbing for a debt from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman holding a deposit claims she grabbed it for a debt during the owner's lifetime.

steps.title: רב נחמן asks if the owner ever demanded the bag while alive
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks whether she has witnesses that the owner demanded the bag during his life and she refused. She says no.
steps.simpleTranslation: She came before רב נחמן. He asked her: Do you have witnesses that he demanded it from you while he was alive and you did not give it to him? She said: No.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן checks whether there is proof that her grab really happened while the owner was alive. This sets up his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply holding a deposit is not a grab, because she was holding it with the owner's permission. Her grab would only be proven if the owner asked for it back during his life and she refused. Without witnesses to that, there is no proof she ever took it as payment while he was alive.

keyTerms.meaning: You did not give it to him

steps.confusionAlert: Why ask about the owner demanding the bag? A deposit sits with her by permission, so only refusing his demand shows she was holding it against him as payment.

phrases.english: She came before Rav Naḥman.
He said to her: Do you have witnesses
that it was demanded from you during his lifetime
and you did not give it to him?
She said to him: No.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִית לִיךְ סָהֲדֵי דְּתַבְעוּהָ מִינִּיךְ מֵחַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The judge tests the woman's claim from step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether there are witnesses that she refused the owner's demand during his life

steps.title: Her grab counts as after death, so it is worthless
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that without proof, her grab counts as a תפיסה after death, and a תפיסה after death is worth nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it is a grabbing after death, and grabbing after death is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives his ruling: the woman loses and must return the bag to the יורשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since nothing shows she held the bag against the owner while he lived, her grab only counts from after his death. By then the property already belonged to the יורשים. This applies the same rule of רב נחמן quoted by רבא in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: Grabbing done after the debtor has died
It is nothing (it has no legal effect)

steps.whatToRemember: Grabbing property for a debt works only during the debtor's lifetime. If someone holding a deposit cannot prove she held it against the owner while he lived, her grab counts as after death and is worthless.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, הָוֵי תְּפִיסָה דִּלְאַחַר מִיתָה,
phrases.english: If so, it is a grabbing after death,

phrases.aramaic: וּתְפִיסָה דִּלְאַחַר מִיתָה — לֹא כְּלוּם הִיא.
phrases.english: and grabbing after death is nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, הָוֵי תְּפִיסָה דִּלְאַחַר מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the case using the 'no witnesses' answer from step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Without proof that she refused the owner while he was alive, the woman's hold on the deposit is a תפיסה after death and has no effect. The יורשים get the bag.

steps.title: רבא reverses an oath because of a trusted report
steps.stepSummary: A woman was obligated to take a שבועה in רבא's court. בת רב חסדא told רבא the woman is suspected of swearing falsely, so רבא moved the oath to the other side.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman was obligated to take an oath in רבא's court. The daughter of רב חסדא said to him: I know that she is suspected of swearing falsely. So רבא reversed the oath onto the other side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story in which רבא changed who takes the oath, based on one trusted person's report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the woman would swear and be free of paying. Because רבא trusted בת רב חסדא's report, he did not let a suspected person swear. Instead the other side swears and collects.

keyTerms.meaning: He reversed it (turned the oath over)

phrases.english: A certain woman who was obligated to take an oath
in Rava's court.
The daughter of Rav Chisda said to him:
I know about her that she is suspected of swearing falsely.
Rava reversed the oath onto the opposing party.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story with a new topic: relying on a trusted individual in court.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a trusted person tells the judge that a litigant is suspected of swearing falsely, the oath is moved to the other side.

steps.title: רב פפא says a document was already paid
steps.stepSummary: A document came before רבא, and רב פפא told him he knows the debt in it was already paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once, רב פפא and רב אדא בר מתנא were sitting before רבא. A certain document was brought to him. רב פפא said to him: I know about this document that it has been paid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second story. It sets up a case where only one person, רב פפא, says the document is paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the debt was already paid, the document should not be used to collect again. The question this story raises is whether one person's word is enough to cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: A legal document (here, a loan document)

phrases.english: Once they were sitting before him

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa and Rav Adda bar Mattana,
they brought a certain document before him.
Rav Pappa said to him:
I know about this document that it is paid.

steps.triggerLanguage: זִימְנִין הָווּ יָתְבִי קַמֵּיהּ רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story, also in רבא's court, about relying on one person's word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: a single person testifies that a document is paid.

steps.title: רבא asks if anyone else knows
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב פפא whether another person can testify with him. רב פפא says no.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Is there another person with you? He said: No.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a clarifying question: is רב פפא the only witness?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses are needed to prove something in court. רבא wants to know if there is a second witness to join רב פפא. The answer is no, so רב פפא stands alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Together with the Master (a polite way to say 'you')

phrases.english: He said to him: Is there another person
with the Master?
He said to him: No.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the case from the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether there is a second witness alongside רב פפא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No, רב פפא is the only one.

steps.title: רבא rules that one witness is not enough
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that even though רב פפא is a great person, a single witness is worth nothing here.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Even though you, the Master, are here, one witness is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his ruling: he will not cancel the document based on רב פפא alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule is that one witness cannot take money away or cancel a document. רבא applies that rule even to a respected scholar.
steps.confusionAlert: This seems to clash with the first story, where רבא acted on one woman's word. The next steps deal with exactly this question.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיכָּא מָר,
phrases.english: He said to him: Even though there is the Master,
one witness is nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling, based on the answer that there is no second witness.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A single witness cannot cancel a document, even if he is a great scholar.

steps.title: רב אדא asks why רב פפא is trusted less than רב חסדא's daughter
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנא challenges רבא: you relied on בת רב חסדא alone, so why not on רב פפא?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנא said to him: Should רב פפא not be like the daughter of רב חסדא?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא challenges רבא by pointing out that his two rulings seem inconsistent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first story, רבא acted on one person's word, and that person was a woman, who normally cannot testify. Here he refuses to act on one male scholar. The question is phrased as a question, but it works as a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the daughter of רב חסדא

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יְהֵא רַב פָּפָּא כְּבַת רַב חִסְדָּא?
phrases.english: And should Rav Pappa not be like the daughter of Rav Chisda?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יְהֵא רַב פָּפָּא כְּבַת רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 19 by comparing it to step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that רב פפא's single testimony is worth nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבא relied on one woman's word, he should surely rely on one great scholar.

steps.title: רבא explains that he knows her with certainty
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that he is personally certain בת רב חסדא is truthful, but he does not have that same certainty about רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The daughter of רב חסדא, I know her with certainty. You, Master, I do not know with that certainty.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by explaining the difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ruling was not based on formal testimony. It was based on רבא's own complete certainty about the person. He trusted בת רב חסדא that way, but he could not say the same about רב פפא, so the normal rule of one witness applied.

keyTerms.meaning: I know her with certainty (I fully trust her truthfulness)

steps.whatToRemember: A judge may act on 'קים לי בגויה', meaning personal, total certainty about someone's honesty, even where formal testimony would not be enough.

phrases.aramaic: בַּת רַב חִסְדָּא קִים לִי בְּגַוַּוהּ,
phrases.english: The daughter of Rav Chisda, I know her with certainty;
phrases.notes: רבא is the one answering here, even though the text doesn't name him.

phrases.english: the Master, I do not know him with certainty.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּת רַב חִסְדָּא קִים לִי בְּגַוַּוהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: personal certainty versus formal testimony.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first ruling was based on בת רב חסדא as a single witness, so any respected single witness should count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first ruling rested on רבא's complete personal certainty about her, which he does not have about רב פפא.

steps.title: רב פפא would tear a document on his trusted son's word
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא learns from רבא that personal certainty counts. He says that on the word of his son אבא מר, whom he fully trusts, he would tear up a document.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Now that the Master said that 'I know him with certainty' is a real consideration, then for example, my son אבא מר, whom I know with certainty, I would tear up a document on his word.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא takes רבא's answer and turns it into a practical rule he can use himself as a judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבא treated personal certainty as legally meaningful, רב פפא applies it in his own court. If his son, whom he completely trusts, said a document was paid, he would tear the document up. Tearing it means it can no longer be used to collect.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a real thing (it carries weight)
I would tear up the document

steps.whatToRemember: Personal certainty in someone's truthfulness ('קים לי בגויה') carries real weight for a judge. The next steps correct how far it goes: it can weaken a document, not tear it up.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבא's answer was not just a defense of one ruling. It became a usable principle for how a judge may act.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Now that the Master has said
that "I know him with certainty" is a real consideration,
for example, Abba Mar my son,
whom I know with certainty,
I would tear up a document on his word.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר מָר קִים לִי בְּגַוֵּויהּ מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical conclusion from רבא's answer in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge may tear up a document on the word of someone he knows with certainty is truthful.

steps.title: Can a document really be torn on one witness's word?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's claim that he would tear up a document on the word of his son אבא מר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Would I really tear it up? Can that enter your mind?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to what רב פפא said in the last step. Tearing up a document because of one witness seems impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A document signed by two witnesses is strong evidence. One witness, however trusted, cannot fully cancel it. So the wording 'I would tear it' cannot be right as it stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Can it enter your mind? (a strong rhetorical question)

phrases.english: I would tear it? Can that enter your mind?!
phrases.notes: This goes back to רב פפא's words about his son אבא מר in the step just before this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of רב פפא's statement in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that he would tear up a document on his son's word
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One witness cannot fully cancel a document that two witnesses signed.

steps.title: Not tearing, only weakening the document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording: on the trusted son's word, רב פפא would only weaken the document.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: I would weaken the document on his word.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רב פפא's statement. He would not tear up the document. He would only make it weaker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Personal certainty about one witness is not enough to destroy a document. It is enough to make the judge cautious, so he would not let the document collect payment without more proof.
steps.whatToRemember: A trusted single witness can weaken a document, but cannot tear it up.

phrases.english: Rather: I would weaken the document on his word.
phrases.notes: The document still exists, but he wouldn't let it collect payment without more proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 by correcting the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא would tear up the document on one trusted witness
steps.terutzMaskana: He would only weaken the document, not destroy it

steps.title: A woman owes an oath, and the other side asks for a public oath
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins. A woman must swear in the court of רב ביבי בר אביי, and her opponent asks that she swear in the town so shame might make her admit the truth.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman was obligated to take an oath in the court of רב ביבי בר אביי. The opposing litigant said to the judges: Let her come and swear in the town. Maybe she will be ashamed and admit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story and sets up the case. Her opponent asks for the oath to be taken in public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opponent hopes the public setting will shame her. If she is lying, she might admit the truth instead of swearing falsely. This sets up her counter-demand in the next step.

phrases.english: A certain woman who was obligated to take an oath

phrases.aramaic: בֵּי דִינָא דְּרַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי.
phrases.english: in the court of רב ביבי בר אביי.
The opposing litigant said to them:
Let her come and take the oath in the town,
maybe she will be ashamed and admit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about court documents and timing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: a woman owes an oath, and her opponent wants it taken publicly.

steps.title: She asks for a document of rights first, and רב ביבי agrees
steps.stepSummary: The woman agrees to swear in town only if the court first writes her a document of rights. רב ביבי בר אביי tells them to write it.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to them: Write me a document of rights, so that when I swear, they will give it to me. רב ביבי בר אביי said to them: Write it for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The woman sets a condition, and רב ביבי בר אביי rules in her favor. This ruling is what the next step will attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She wants proof of her win ready ahead of time, so she gets it the moment she swears. The problem is that the court would be writing 'she won' before she has actually sworn.

keyTerms.meaning: a document of rights, a written ruling in her favor

phrases.english: She said to them: Write me a document of rights,
so that when I take the oath, they will give it to me.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי: כִּתְבוּ לַהּ.
phrases.english: רב ביבי בר אביי said to them: Write it for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with her demand and the judge's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ביבי בר אביי allows the court to write the document of rights before the oath.

steps.title: רב פפי sharply rejects the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי mocks רב ביבי's ruling with a wordplay on his family's origin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said: Because you come from unfortunate people, you say unfortunate things?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי attacks רב ביבי בר אביי's ruling as clearly wrong. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a sharp rhetorical challenge, not a real question. רב פפי holds that the ruling to write the document early is a mistake, and he backs this up right after with a statement of רבא.

phrases.english: רב פפי said:
Because you come from unfortunate people,
phrases.notes: A wordplay. רב ביבי's family came from the house of עלי, a line known for dying young.

phrases.english: you say unfortunate things?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פַּפֵּי: מִשּׁוּם דְּאָתֵיתוּ מִמּוּלָאֵי אָמְרִיתוּ מִילֵּי מוּלְיָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ביבי בר אביי's ruling to write the document of rights before the oath
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling is clearly wrong. The reason is given in the next step from רבא.

steps.title: רבא: a judges' approval written too early is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי cites רבא: if judges write their approval on a document before witnesses confirm their signatures, the approval is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבא say: A judges' approval written on a document before the witnesses testified about their signatures is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי brings a proof from רבא to show that רב ביבי's ruling was wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Judges normally confirm a document only after hearing the witnesses vouch for their own signatures. If the judges write the confirmation first, it is invalid, even if the witnesses confirm afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: the judges' written approval of a document

phrases.english: Didn't רבא say:
This approval of judges that was written

phrases.aramaic: מִקַּמֵּי דְּנַחְווֹ סָהֲדֵי אַחֲתִימוּת יְדַיְיהוּ — פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.english: before the witnesses testified about their signatures is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind רב פפי's attack in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: That a court may not write a document of rights before the oath
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling that an approval written before the witnesses testify is invalid

steps.title: Writing it early looks like a lie
steps.stepSummary: The reason behind רבא's rule is that it looks like a lie. The same applies to writing the woman's document before she swears.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see it looks like a lie. Here too, it looks like a lie.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי pulls out the reason behind רבא's rule and applies it to the woman's case. This closes his argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A court document that states something before it has happened looks false. A document of rights written before her oath claims she won before she actually swore. So the court should not write it ahead of time.
steps.whatToRemember: This is רב פפי's argument: writing the document of rights before the oath looks like a lie (מיחזי כשיקרא). The next step (step 30) rejects רבא's rule that this argument rests on.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes רב פפי's attack on רב ביבי בר אביי. The גמרא then tests whether רבא's rule really holds, and in step 30 it decides that it does not.

phrases.english: So we see it looks like a lie,
here too, it looks like a lie.
phrases.notes: Here too means the woman's document, written before she has actually sworn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא מִיחְזֵי כְּשִׁיקְרָא, הָכִי נָמֵי מִיחְזֵי כְּשִׁיקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the reason from רבא's rule in step 28 and applies it to the case in step 26.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רב פפי, the court should not have written the document of rights before the woman swore, because it looks like a lie. The next step (step 30) rejects the rule of רבא that this rests on.

steps.title: רבא's rule is not accepted because of רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's rule. It quotes רב נחמן, who reports that רבי מאיר holds a גט found in the garbage, then signed and given, is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא's rule is not accepted, because of what רב נחמן said. רב נחמן said: רבי מאיר used to say that even if a man found a גט in the garbage, had it signed and gave it to his wife, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now rejects רבא's rule that רב פפי used against רב ביבי. It brings רבי מאיר's view that a document written earlier, for no particular purpose, can still be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that writing something before it is true looks like a lie. רבי מאיר holds that a document written long before it is signed and used is still valid. So the time of writing does not matter, and רבא's concern falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is not so. The rule is not accepted.
And he had it signed by witnesses

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the writing of a document with the signing of it. רבי מאיר's point is that the text can be written at any time, even with no purpose in mind. The witnesses' signing is what makes it work.

phrases.english: And it is not accepted, because of Rav Nachman.
phrases.notes: 'It' is רבא's rule from the last steps, about not writing the court's approval too early.

phrases.english: For Rav Nachman said:
Rabbi Meir used to say:
Even if he found it in a garbage heap
phrases.notes: "It" is a גט that already had names matching his and his wife's, written by someone else.

phrases.english: and had it signed and gave it to her, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the rule of רבא that רב פפי cited against רב ביבי בר אביי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's rule that writing a document before the fact it records is invalid
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי מאיר holds that the time of writing does not matter. Even a document written with no purpose can later be signed and used.

steps.title: The Rabbis disagree only about a גט
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן adds that the רבנן argue with רבי מאיר only about a גט, which must be written for the woman's sake. For all other documents they agree with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even the רבנן disagree with רבי מאיר only about a גט, because a גט must be written for the sake of the woman. But for other documents they agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן limits the argument between רבי מאיר and the רבנן to a גט. This means that for ordinary documents, everyone agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think רבא could follow the רבנן. But the רבנן's only reason to argue is the special rule of לשמה, which applies only to a גט. For other documents, everyone holds that the time of writing makes no difference. So no one is left to support רבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Writing for her sake. A גט must be written specifically for this woman.
Other documents, like loans and sales

steps.whyThisMatters: This turns רבי מאיר's single opinion into a view everyone accepts for regular documents. That is what knocks out רבא's rule and supports רב ביבי's ruling.

phrases.english: And even the Rabbis do not disagree
with Rabbi Meir
except regarding women's divorce documents,
since we need the writing to be for her sake,
but for other documents they agree with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבָּנַן לָא פְּלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רב נחמן's statement so that it reflects everyone's view for ordinary documents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The only disagreement concerns a גט, because of לשמה. For other documents, all agree that when a document was written does not matter.

steps.title: Proof from a loan document that was repaid
steps.stepSummary: The proof that the רבנן agree about other documents comes from רבי יוחנן. A loan document that was repaid cannot be reused for a new loan, because its lien was already canceled.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a document that someone borrowed with and then repaid may not be used again for a new loan, because its lien has already been canceled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove that the רבנן agree with רבי מאיר about ordinary documents. The source is רבי יוחנן's rule about reusing a loan document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן forbids reusing a repaid loan document. The reason he gives is that the lien was canceled once the loan was paid. He does not say the reason is that the document was written before the second loan. That choice of reason will be the key to the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: He may not borrow with it again
Its lien, the lender's claim on the borrower's property

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: For Rav Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
A document that one borrowed with and repaid
he may not borrow with it again,
because its lien has already been canceled.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim that the רבנן agree with רבי מאיר about ordinary documents.
steps.raayaObject: That for ordinary documents, the time of writing does not invalidate them
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's rule that a repaid loan document cannot be reused because its lien was canceled

steps.title: Inference from רבי יוחנן's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא focuses on רבי יוחנן's reason. The document is barred only because the lien was canceled, not because it looks like something written early. The sentence continues in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is only that its lien was canceled. But as for the fact that it looks like...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its proof by pointing to the exact reason רבי יוחנן gave. The sentence is cut off here and finishes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן gave only one reason: the lien was canceled. That implies the concern that the document looks like it was written before the loan is not a problem. This is the opposite of רבא's concern that early writing looks like a lie.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is. It introduces an inference from the reason given.
To appear, or as for how it looks

phrases.english: The reason is that its lien was canceled,
but as for appearing
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going in the next part of the text. It will say that merely looking like a lie is not a problem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the exact reason רבי יוחנן gave in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: That 'looking like a lie' does not invalidate an ordinary document
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's choice of 'the lien was canceled' as his only reason
